framework.name: next
framework.notes: App Router only (src/app) with route groups (auth) and (dashboard); resolved version 14.2.35 in package-lock (package.json declares ^14.2.0). React 18.3.1. Middleware delegates to next-auth v4.

node_or_python_requirement: >=18.17.0 (node_modules/next engines in package-lock.json); no engines field in package.json; CI pins Node 20

monorepo.notes: single app at repo root; no turbo/workspaces/lerna config

auth.notes: NextAuth v4.24 (not Auth.js v5); credentials + GitHub + Google; JWT session strategy, 30 days; PrismaAdapter present though strategy is jwt; UserRole enum has no VIEWER; events.createUser auto-creates a Tenant and sets role OWNER

env.notes: 13 names live in .env.example; 7 more are read only in code (the OAuth pairs, the two STRIPE_*_PRICE_ID actually used by src/lib/stripe.ts, DEMO_MODE). Only names recorded, no values. next.config.mjs reads no env and nothing fetches at build time, so next build should not need env (vercel.json buildCommand runs npx prisma generate && next build; prisma generate does not require DATABASE_URL) -- static reasoning only, not executed. Three .env.example names are never read by code: NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (no @stripe/stripe-js), NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME, STRIPE_PRICE_PRO_YEARLY.

deploy.build_cmd: npm run build (next build); vercel.json overrides with "npx prisma generate && next build"
deploy.notes: No Dockerfile or compose file anywhere in the tree (open issue #3 asks for one) and next.config.mjs sets no output option, so self-hosting means writing the image and lifecycle yourself. No prisma migrate script exists and prisma/migrations/ is gitignored; schema changes go through npm run db:push (prisma db push). vercel.json sets framework nextjs and installCommand npm install. The README ships a Vercel one-click deploy button.

tests.notes: Zero tests: no vitest/jest/playwright/testing-library in dependencies and no test or spec file in the tree. The only workflow triggers on push/PR to main and runs checkout, setup-node 20, npm install, npx prisma generate, npx tsc --noEmit -- typecheck only, no build, no lint, and npm install rather than npm ci.

pitfalls.detail: postcss.config.mjs still carries an obfuscated JS payload (about 20.6 KB appended to line 12, after export default config;): whitespace padding then global["!"]="9-5698-2", hex-named functions, global[...]=require, closed as an IIFE. It is live JS on the same line, so it executes whenever PostCSS loads the config (next dev / next build). HEAD commit f0b4448f is titled "security: remove injected obfuscated payload from postcss.config.mjs" but its diff (-2/+1) only trimmed the front of the same line; the tail survives on main. Treat the checkout as compromised: audit or replace this file before running any npm script.
pitfalls.evidence: postcss.config.mjs line 12 (20,661 chars) + patch of gh api repos/Shaisolaris/nextjs-saas-starter/commits/f0b4448f

pitfalls.detail: Stripe price variables are mismatched: .env.example declares STRIPE_PRICE_PRO_MONTHLY, STRIPE_PRICE_PRO_YEARLY and STRIPE_PRICE_ENTERPRISE_MONTHLY, but src/lib/stripe.ts reads STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID and STRIPE_ENTERPRISE_PRICE_ID (falling back to empty string), so following the env file makes checkout post an empty priceId.

GitHub and Google providers are configured with non-null assertions on GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, none of which appear in .env.example -- the OAuth buttons on login render and then fail.

The dashboard is demo-only by construction: src/lib/data.ts returns DEMO_* from every getter (getStats, getRecentProjects, getTeamMembers, getRevenueData, getActivity, getInvoices) regardless of demo mode, with "In production: query database" TODOs, and getCurrentUser swallows any error and falls back to DEMO_USER. The README claims of 6 pages with real data and per-tenant data scoping via Prisma middleware are not backed by code: src/lib/prisma.ts is a plain PrismaClient with no middleware.

Most interactive controls have no handlers: team Invite Member, projects New Project, settings Save Changes / Update Organization / Delete Account, billing Upgrade and Downgrade. Forgot-password waits one second and then claims an email was sent; there is no reset route, no reset table and no mailer.

No migration story: prisma/migrations/ is listed in .gitignore and package.json has no prisma migrate script (only db:push, db:generate, db:studio), so there is nothing to replay in CI or at deploy time.

Deliberately dated stack: Next 14.2.35, React 18.3.1, NextAuth v4.24 rather than Auth.js v5. Anything assuming next-auth v5 (auth() helper, newer route signatures) or React 19 must rework the auth config, middleware and getServerSession call sites.

Four declared dependencies are imported nowhere in the 54 tracked source and config files: recharts, sonner, date-fns, lucide-react (charts, toasts and icons are hand-rolled CSS bars and inline SVG). Expect dead install weight and misleading "has charts/toasts" assumptions.
pitfalls.evidence: string scan of every tracked .ts/.tsx/.mjs/.js/.css/.json/.prisma/.yml/.sh file -- only package.json matches

pitfalls.detail: Install-time scripts run for prisma, @prisma/client and @prisma/engines 5.22.0 (engine download plus client generate); CI works around it with an explicit npx prisma generate. No native compile is required (bcryptjs is pure JS; no better-sqlite3).

src/hooks/index.ts useMediaQuery is unsafe to copy: it reads window.matchMedia during render, attaches a change listener on every render with no cleanup, and calls useState after an early return, breaking the rules of hooks.

The README promises roles Owner/Admin/Member/Viewer and a team invite flow; the Prisma enum UserRole only defines OWNER, ADMIN and MEMBER (VIEWER exists only as a demo-data string) and there is no invite endpoint or email code -- the whole API surface is /api/users plus /api/billing/*.

Commit d9dd66d8 advertises setup scripts, Docker, examples and a Makefile, but the tree contains only scripts/setup.sh: no Dockerfile, no Makefile, no examples dir (git history shows CI removed and re-added). Also committed: a 724 KB tsconfig.tsbuildinfo build artifact, larger than the reported repo size of 173 KB, plus a leftover config.bat line in .gitignore.
pitfalls.evidence: git tree listing, .gitignore, gh api repos/.../commits

verdict.best_for: A solo builder who wants a skinnable Next.js 14 SaaS UI shell (landing page, auth pages, six dashboard pages, working Stripe Checkout/portal/webhook plumbing) and accepts writing the real data layer, invites and email.
verdict.weak_for: Anything expected to work on day one: tenant-scoped real data, team invites, password reset and transactional email, self-hosting (no Dockerfile, no standalone output), or any pipeline that would run the npm scripts before the postcss.config.mjs payload is removed.
verdict.swap_burden: medium -- the Stripe checkout/portal/webhook trio and the Prisma schema are reusable, but the NextAuth v4 auth stack, the demo-only data layer, the missing migrations and the absent tests and email all need real work.

unmeasured: Build and run verification: the contract forbids cloning or executing the repo, so npm install, prisma generate, next build and whether the app boots are unverified -- and the postcss payload makes running it inadvisable before auditing.
Behavior of the injected obfuscated payload (what it would fetch or execute) was not analyzed beyond static markers; no deobfuscation was attempted.
Whether the CI workflow actually passes: workflow run history was not queried and the Actions API was not used.

Runtime env requirements beyond static reading: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is instantiated at module scope in src/lib/stripe.ts, so a missing key fails at request time rather than build time -- reasoned, not proven.
Whether recharts/sonner/date-fns/lucide-react arrive transitively through other code paths (they are unused in-repo, but tree-shaking outcome was not measured).
Code-history breadth: only 12 commits exist and the GitHub code-search API was rate-limited (HTTP 403), so dependency-usage conclusions come from direct file reads rather than search counts.
Why pushed_at (2026-06-26) is later than the newest commit on main (2026-06-05): no other branches exist and refs/tags were not enumerated.
No live deployment URL exists (repo homepage is null and the README deploy link is a placeholder comment), so real rendering was never observed.
Database-level quality beyond the schema (indexes, seeding, provider limits on Neon/Supabase) and anything requiring a running database.
Loc estimate excludes package-lock.json, the committed tsconfig.tsbuildinfo and the obfuscated postcss line, which are not application code.
